tasks.short: Analyze treatment data to assess art-therapy effectiveness

steps.what: Define the actual treatment question, comparable outcomes and appropriate observation periods
inputs: actual treatment approaches and evaluation question
existing outcome definitions and collection protocol

steps.what: Select and check existing treatment and outcome records, resolving missing values and incompatible measures explicitly
inputs: authorized existing treatment and outcome records
outputs: therapist-checked analysis table with missingness and comparability flags

steps.what: Calculate specified outcome changes, denominators and descriptive comparisons with fixed formulas
inputs: therapist-checked analysis table with missingness and comparability flags
outputs: reproducible comparison tables with explicit denominators and missingness

steps.what: Verify calculated comparisons against source cases and interpret treatment effectiveness without treating association as proof of causation
inputs: reproducible comparison tables with explicit denominators and missingness
therapist-checked analysis table with missingness and comparability flags
outputs: therapist's checked effectiveness interpretation with uncertainty

steps.what: Write and finish checking the analysis record with actual comparisons, limitations and interpretation
inputs: therapist's checked effectiveness interpretation with uncertainty
reproducible comparison tables with explicit denominators and missingness

steps.what: Save the checked analysis record in the existing document store

tasks.design: Use fixed formulas in {SPREADSHEET} on the therapist-checked table from {OPS_SYSTEM}. The therapist checks denominators and sample cases, interprets the actual results and authors the analysis in {DOCS}; no model infers effectiveness from art images or missing outcomes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated descriptive calculations can require manual arithmetic or rebuilding the same formulas.
tasks.enabler_now: A versioned formula workbook can reproduce specified comparisons and expose missingness.
tasks.still_hard: Interpret sparse or noncomparable outcomes and avoid unsupported causal conclusions.
tasks.human_edge: Judge what the data can support clinically.

ambition.what: Repeat the same defined evaluation when genuinely comparable new outcome data arrives.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-7; treatment-data access and clinical governance consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: fixed spreadsheet formulas can compute descriptive treatment outcome comparisons; clinical effectiveness interpretation depends on data quality and study limitations.

assumptions: OPS_SYSTEM is the existing therapy record. Actual clinicians and existing outcome collection produce treatment/outcome data before this task; s2 explicitly counts selection, cleaning and comparability checks. No new questionnaire capture is hidden.

Use existing export and native spreadsheet formulas first. No language model for arithmetic or clinical conclusions. If equivalent formulas already exist, the calculation step is already assisted and earns no new saving.
Shares are unmeasured provisional scenarios. Gross 25 minus 2 workbook and definition upkeep gives 23 net. Source and result checking remain; same-system save is 1% fully retained.
unknowns: Actual outcome comparability, missingness and current calculation workflow
research_questions: Can the existing records support a reproducible comparison, and how much actual arithmetic is still repeated manually?

already_counted.description: Check source table, calculated comparisons and clinical interpretation

incremental.description: Maintain formula definitions and regression checks on sample cases

approvals.approved_version: complete analysis record checked at end of s5; edits void check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero if equivalent formulas already used or data unusable; cautious range below provisional 23% net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Instruct individuals or groups in the use of art media

steps.what: Explain and demonstrate the use of the actual art media at a level suitable for the individuals or group
inputs: actual paint, clay, yarn or other selected media

steps.what: Observe actual media use, help with difficulties and adapt instruction to participant responses
inputs: participants' actual media use and responses
outputs: actual instruction adaptations and participant responses observed

steps.what: Write and check the normal therapy-session note covering actual media instruction and participant response
inputs: actual instruction adaptations and participant responses observed

steps.what: Save the checked session note in the same therapy record

tasks.design: Use native session headings and identifiers in {OPS_SYSTEM} for the normal therapy note. Actual explanation, demonstration and responsive support remain in person, and the therapist supplies all observations in the checked note.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated session metadata and formatting may add entry work.
tasks.enabler_now: Native therapy-session templates can supply headings without inventing participant responses.
tasks.still_hard: Adapt hands-on instruction to actual physical, cognitive or emotional needs.
tasks.human_edge: Notice difficulty and support the participant appropriately.

ambition.what: Reduce small note-formatting work while retaining direct media instruction.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: art-therapy sessions can include media instruction and a clinical session note; native templates organize notes without observing participant response.

assumptions: OPS_SYSTEM is the existing therapy record. Scenario is instruction within a documented therapy session; confirm note ownership to avoid counting the same session note in another task.

Therapist produces actual instruction and observations in s1-s2, then captures them in s3. Native headings first, no recording or generated clinical content. An unrecorded standalone demonstration has no note saving.
Shares are unmeasured provisional scenarios. Gross 0.9 minus 0.2 upkeep gives 0.7 net. Same-system save is 1% fully retained and ordinary checking stays inside note authoring.
unknowns: Actual session-note ownership and native template availability
research_questions: Does the normal note contain repeated formatting, and is this instruction already documented by a separately counted session task?

already_counted.description: Capture and check actual instruction and response

approvals.approved_version: complete session note checked at end of s3; edits void check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero if no distinct note or existing template sufficient; cautious range below provisional 0.7% net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Supervise staff, volunteers, practicum students and interns

steps.what: Review actual assigned work and supervision objectives for the staff member, volunteer or trainee
inputs: actual assigned work and trainee submissions
outputs: supervisor's source-checked work review and supervision priorities

steps.what: Observe actual practice and identify difficulties, boundaries or support needs
inputs: supervisor's source-checked work review and supervision priorities

steps.what: Discuss the observed work, give feedback and agree appropriate next steps with the supervised person
inputs: supervisor's source-checked work review and supervision priorities
outputs: actual supervision feedback and agreed next steps

steps.what: Write and check the existing practicum supervision record with actual observations and agreed next steps
inputs: actual supervision feedback and agreed next steps

steps.what: Save the checked supervision record in the same learning record

tasks.design: Configure a native supervision view in {LMS} linking actual submissions and objectives from {DOCS}. The therapist reviews and observes work, gives feedback and records actual supervision; the view does not rate a trainee or infer competence.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supervision sources can require repeated navigation across submissions and objectives.
tasks.enabler_now: Native trainee views can link existing work to the correct supervision objectives.
tasks.still_hard: Understand actual practice and provide useful, fair feedback.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize support needs and discuss professional boundaries.

ambition.what: Improve source access without automating supervision judgements.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: practicum supervision combines work review, observation, feedback and a supervision record; native learning views can link existing submissions and objectives.

assumptions: Scenario is recorded practicum/intern supervision, one of the statement's populations. LMS is its existing learning record; actual supervised people produce submissions and supervisor produces observations and feedback.
Native view first. No new behavior capture, automatic performance score or inferred completion. Ordinary supervision record authoring remains; no separate self-approval step.

Shares are unmeasured provisional scenarios. Gross 2 minus 0.3 view upkeep gives 1.7 net. Other supervised populations require their actual record process; same-system save remains fully retained at 1%.
unknowns: Current supervision sources and actual navigation burden
research_questions: Can native links reduce source navigation without introducing monitoring or automatic competence judgements?

approvals.approved_version: complete actual supervision record checked at end of s4; edits void check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero if native supervision view already sufficient; cautious range below provisional 1.7% net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Conduct information-sharing sessions and in-service workshops

steps.what: Adapt and finish checking actual workshop material for the intended professional, client or community audience
inputs: existing approved art-therapy information and workshop material

steps.what: Save the checked workshop material in the existing document project
Conduct the information-sharing session or in-service workshop and adapt the explanation to the audience
Answer actual audience questions and clarify the scope and limitations of the information
outputs: actual questions addressed and limitations explained

tasks.design: Use native reusable workshop sections and layouts in {DOCS} for a session that actually requires adapted material. The therapist checks the audience-specific content and conducts the session and questions directly; no notices, attendance record or post-session report are invented.
tasks.previous_blocker: Adapting an actual workshop can repeat layout and approved introductory content.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document templates and reusable sections can preserve approved content while the therapist adapts examples.
tasks.still_hard: Make the information useful to this audience and answer unexpected questions.
tasks.human_edge: Read the room and explain the limits of art-therapy information.

ambition.what: Reduce repeated material setup while keeping live information sharing.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: reusable document sections can reduce repeated workshop layout while audience adaptation and live delivery remain human work.

assumptions: Scenario is preparation and delivery of an actual workshop with adapted material, not recurring attendance at an already prepared session. Existing content authors supply approved information; therapist supplies adaptation and checks it in s1.

Native reuse first. No model-generated clinical claims or inferred audience understanding. If material preparation belongs to another task or the workshop is already ready, remove that baseline and claim no setup saving.
Shares are unmeasured provisional scenarios. Gross 2.4 minus 0.3 content/template upkeep gives 2.1 net. Same-system save is 1% fully retained, and final content checking is inside normal preparation.
unknowns: Actual workshop material ownership and repeated layout work
research_questions: Does an actual workshop require repeated preparation that native sections can remove without counting another task's content work?

already_counted.description: Adapt and check actual workshop material

approvals.approved_version: complete audience-specific workshop material checked at end of s1; edits void check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero if material already ready or counted elsewhere; cautious range below provisional 2.1% net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

reach: Record administrators configure existing views; therapists retain treatment interpretation, instruction and supervision.
skills_to_grow: Keep actual observations distinct from inferred responses
Reuse approved material without copied clinical claims
role.ambitious_version: Make outcome analysis reproducible and reduce verified repeated record or material setup while retaining therapeutic judgement and live teaching.
